related_questions.question: Do you need to be vaccinated to go to French Polynesia?

text_blocks.snippet: French Polynesia currently has no COVID-19 related entry requirements for travelers, regardless of origin or vaccination status. However, it's crucial to check for requirements at any transit locations, like the United States, and with your airline or travel provider. Additionally, some routine vaccinations are recommended, and a yellow fever vaccination certificate may be required depending on your itinerary.

list.title: COVID-19:

list.title: Yellow Fever:
list.snippet: An official yellow fever vaccination certificate is required if you are traveling from a country with a risk of yellow fever transmission. This also applies to transit stops exceeding 12 hours in risk countries.

list.title: Recommended Routine Vaccinations:

list.title: Other Vaccinations:
list.snippet: TravelHealthPro recommends considering vaccinations for typhoid and hepatitis A, as these can be transmitted through contaminated food and water.

list.title: Transit Requirements:
list.snippet: Be aware that transit requirements for other destinations, particularly the United States, may differ and travelers should check with the relevant authorities for those locations.
Always check with your airline, cruise operator, or travel agent for the latest travel requirements.
Consult with your doctor or a travel clinic for personalized recommendations regarding vaccinations and health advice.
Be sure to have a passport valid for at least three months beyond your expected departure date.
While a tourist visa is not required for stays up to 90 days, be aware of any other potential entry requirements or restrictions.

related_questions.question: Is it safe to travel to Tahiti right now?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, it is generally safe to travel to Tahiti right now, with "normal precautions" being advised. While petty crime is low, it's always wise to be aware of your surroundings and take precautions, especially in tourist areas.
snippet_highlighted_words: Yes, it is generally safe to travel to Tahiti right now, with "normal precautions" being advised

list.title: Low Crime Rate:
list.snippet: French Polynesia, including Tahiti, has a low crime rate, particularly petty crime.

list.title: Petty Theft:
list.snippet: While violent crime is rare, petty theft, like pickpocketing, can occur in Papeete, especially in crowded areas.

list.title: Water Safety:
list.snippet: Beaches are not patrolled, and strong currents can be present, even in lagoons. Be cautious, ask locals for advice, and follow any warning signs.

list.title: Natural Hazards:
list.snippet: Be aware of the potential for cyclones and tropical storms, especially during the November to April cyclone season. Earthquakes and tsunamis are also a possibility, so be familiar with evacuation plans.

list.title: Be aware of your surroundings:
list.snippet: Take normal precautions with your belongings, especially in Papeete and tourist areas.

list.title: Stay informed:
list.snippet: Check weather forecasts and be prepared to adjust your travel plans if needed, especially during cyclone season.

list.title: Follow local advice:
list.snippet: Pay attention to any warnings or advice from local authorities or tourism officials.
